verification-preview-process-ownershipverification-addressing-and-errors0 of 0.375 (minor)failNeither credited mechanism is met. The port is ephemeral and --strictPort is used. But freePort closes its probe server before vite binds, so there is a window in which another server can take the port. The only ownership check is the `exited` flag sampled at the top of each loop iteration, before the request. visual-helper-allow-overlapverification-warnings0.375 of 0.375 (minor)passI&#39;m ruling with judges A and C: pass. The helper supports an explicit allow-overlap marker, and a focused browser test confirms it. How it works: `collectSnapshot` (diagnostics.mjs:47-53) walks each element&#39;s ancestors and records the id of every ancestor that carries `data-presentation-allow-overlap` in `allow`. `findOverlaps` (diagnostics.mjs:96-109) skips any pair whose elements share one of those marked ancestors (`a.allow.some((id) =&gt; b.allow.includes(id))`). `analyzeSnapshot` (127-131) only reports pairs that `findOverlaps` returns. `inspect-presentation.mjs` (52-62) runs the snapshot and analysis on every step, after the settle wait. Focused test: inspect.test.ts builds the `fx-allowed` fixture (line 31). It puts two Labels at identical coordinates inside `&lt;div data-presentation-allow-overlap&gt;`. The test &#39;does not report overlap inside an explicitly allowed subtree&#39; (147-151) runs the real helper against a production build and asserts exit 0 with no WARN lines. The same Labels without the marker (`fx-collision`) do produce a warning naming both texts (137-145), so the marker is what suppresses it. The unit test &#39;exempts pairs inside one allow-overlap subtree only&#39; (diagnostics.test.ts:26-34) checks the same thing at the function level: a marked pair produces no warning, and the identical pair without the marker produces one. Why I&#39;m not ruling with judge B: the material is accurate but does not decide this requirement. B points out that a marked element colliding with an unmarked one is still reported, and diagnostics.test.ts:32 confirms that. But the review guidance only says skipping every pair with at least one marked element is &quot;a correct reading&quot;. It says &quot;do not require the helper to keep reporting collisions between a marked element and an unmarked one&quot;, which makes the one-sided skip acceptable, not mandatory. B misquotes this as &quot;the correct reading&quot;. The fixture scenario is overlap between elements inside the marked subtree. Those collisions are suppressed and tested, and the guidance&#39;s requirement is a focused test that marks an overlapping subtree and gets no warning, which exists. The helper supports an explicit allow-overlap marker, and a focused browser test confirms it. How it works: `collectSnapshot` (diagnostics.mjs:47-53) walks each element&#39;s ancestors and records the id of every ancestor that carries `data-presentation-allow-overlap` in `allow`. `findOverlaps` (diagnostics.mjs:96-109) skips any pair whose elements share one of those marked ancestors (`a.allow.some((id) =&gt; b.allow.includes(id))`). `analyzeSnapshot` (127-131) only reports pairs that `findOverlaps` returns. `inspect-presentation.mjs` (52-62) runs the snapshot and analysis on every step, after the settle wait. Focused test: inspect.test.ts builds the `fx-allowed` fixture (line 31). It puts two Labels at identical coordinates inside `&lt;div data-presentation-allow-overlap&gt;`. The test &#39;does not report overlap inside an explicitly allowed subtree&#39; (147-151) runs the real helper against a production build and asserts exit 0 with no WARN lines. The same Labels without the marker (`fx-collision`) do produce a warning naming both texts (137-145), so the marker is what suppresses it. The unit test &#39;exempts pairs inside one allow-overlap subtree only&#39; (diagnostics.test.ts:26-34) checks the same thing at the function level: a marked pair produces no warning, and the identical pair without the marker produces one. Why I&#39;m not ruling with judge B: the material is accurate but does not decide this requirement. B points out that a marked element colliding with an unmarked one is still reported, and diagnostics.test.ts:32 confirms that. But the review guidance only says skipping every pair with at least one marked element is &quot;a correct reading&quot;. It says &quot;do not require the helper to keep reporting collisions between a marked element and an unmarked one&quot;, which makes the one-sided skip acceptable, not mandatory. B misquotes this as &quot;the correct reading&quot;. The fixture scenario is overlap between elements inside the marked subtree. Those collisions are suppressed and tested, and the guidance&#39;s requirement is a focused test that marks an overlapping subtree and gets no warning, which exists. If readiness fails, startPreview itself awaits stop() before rethrowing. verify.mjs: every path after startPreview goes through main&#39;s try/finally { await preview.stop() }. It rests on a hypothetical rejection from browser.close() inside the finally block. The guidance&#39;s named scenarios are success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, and an error thrown after the preview started. They run verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs as child processes through run(), which wraps execFile with a timeout and resolves only when the process has exited. Assertions run only after that, against exit codes, output and screenshot files. No test calls waitForTimeout or any other sleep. The only setTimeout calls in the tests are fault-injection code written into fixture scene source (verify.e2e.test.ts:116 and :130), not test waits. Where the scripts drive the browser, they wait on observable state before acting: - verify&#39;s waitForIndex polls data-step-index until it leaves i-1, with a deadline, and only then checks the step. - inspect calls page.waitForFunction until data-step-index equals the target step before it captures. Judge C&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. The --settle 1500 delay and verify&#39;s SETTLE_MS are fixed settle windows inside the scripts under test, used for screenshot motion and for attributing browser errors to the right step. Neither is a sleep a test uses in place of waiting for the step index, and in both scripts the step index is confirmed by polling first. The guidance also lists longer fixed settle delays as validator noise. Judges A and B&#39;s reading matches the source.","evidence":["tests/integration/helpers.ts:15-22 run() resolves from the execFile callback when the process exits (with timeout 280000). The two versions of each file are identical. startPreview launches Vite&#39;s own bin/vite.js under process.execPath, so the child process is the preview server itself rather than an npm or npx wrapper. stop() sends SIGTERM, schedules SIGKILL after 3s, and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; promise. If readiness fails, startPreview itself awaits stop() before rethrowing. verify.mjs: every path after startPreview goes through main&#39;s try/finally { await preview.stop() }. That covers success, a failing check (PhaseError thrown from renderRoute), a browser launch failure (launchBrowser is called inside renderRoute, inside that try), and any later error. inspect-presentation.mjs: a launchBrowser rejection is caught and awaits preview.stop() before rethrowing. Every later step (newPage, goto, the waits, screenshots, diagnostics) runs inside try/finally { await browser.close(); await preview.stop() }. Judge C&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. It rests on a hypothetical rejection from browser.close() inside the finally block. The guidance&#39;s named scenarios are success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, and an error thrown after the preview started. The only browser-backed tests in the delivery are the three files in tests/integration. vitest.config.ts:4-5 says browser-backed suites live in their own directory. vitest.integration.config.ts:3-8 includes only tests/integration/**/*.test.ts, and the other projects use jsdom or node. None of these tests drives a browser page itself, and none sleeps. Each one runs verify.mjs, inspect-presentation.mjs or npm through run() (helpers.ts:15-22). run() wraps execFile and resolves only when the child process exits. Every assertion comes after that await and reads final state: the exit code, output text, PNG files, or whether the port is closed (portIsClosed, helpers.ts:51-57). The full files contain no waitForTimeout, sleep or fixed delay: inspect.test.ts lines 1-242, verify.e2e.test.ts lines 1-185 and bootstrap.test.ts lines 1-90. The only setTimeout calls (verify.e2e.test.ts:116,130) are inside fault code the test writes into the scene source. They are not waits in the test. Where the scripts move between steps, they wait on state. inspect uses page.waitForFunction on data-step-index === n with a 5000 ms timeout (inspect-presentation.mjs:46-50). verify uses waitForIndex, which polls data-step-index with a deadline (verify.mjs:38-47, 91-94). Judge C&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. The &#39;--settle 1500&#39; that inspect.test.ts:90 passes is a capture-delay option of the delivered script. The script applies it with waitForTimeout (inspect-presentation.mjs:52) only after waitForFunction has confirmed the step index. Verify&#39;s SETTLE_MS (verify.mjs:100) likewise runs after waitForIndex. Neither one is the test waiting a fixed time for a transition before asserting the step. The test asserts only after the process exits. The guidance also lists longer fixed settle delays as validator noise. The child process is therefore the preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. stop() sends SIGTERM, falls back to SIGKILL after 3s and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; promise. If readiness fails, startPreview awaits stop() before rethrowing. In verify.mjs, main wraps everything after startPreview in try/finally { await preview.stop() }. launchBrowser runs inside renderRoute, which runs inside that try. So success, a failing check (PhaseError), a browser launch failure and any later error all pass through the finally that stops the preview. in order. Observed: `steps.ts` and the rendered headings match the spec table verbatim for all nine steps (checked the `BEATS` array against the spec table, and the `h2` and caption text per step in the DOM). Result: pass."},{"line":2317,"text":"- **Order-derived numbering.** Predicted: number equals position. Observed: the header number and progress item track `nav.index + 1` (`Presentation.tsx:36`). Reorder check (step 8, below): swapping two steps in a copy produced `step 0 Second beat`, `step 1 First beat`, and verify passed. Result: pass."},{"line":2318,"text":"- **Stable entities morph; newcomers enter after settle; departing entity exits.** Predicted: persisting entities keep their DOM node; newcomers fade in after the ~0.65 s delay; departures fade out. Observed (DOM node identity and opacity across all nine transitions): persisting nodes were kept (same element) at every transition; newcomers were created fresh with opacity 0 right after the press and 1.00 after settling. Departure was not exercised by the sample itself (the sample never removes an entity). Departure was exercised in copy `faultC` (entity `first` removed from step 2 onward): the mutation log showed `first` at opacity 1.00 at t+0 ms, fading to 0.00 at about +260 ms, then removed from the DOM, while `second` stayed at 1.00. Result: pass for departure timing; the sample has no departure beat."},{"line":2319,"text":"- **Grouped scene shares one instance.** Predicted: one `groupKey` and one `Scene` keep persisting entities mounted across steps. Observed: persisting nodes were never remounted across steps 1 to 9 (node identity probe). Result: pass."},{"line":2320,"text":"- **Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers.** Predicted: persisting entities stay at full opacity while moving. Observed: opacity 1.00 for every continuing entity at every settled step. The mid-transition value for continuing entities was not sampled finely enough to rule out a brief dip. Result: pass at the settled level; the wrapper question is recorded in the ledger."},{"line":2321,"text":"- **Intentional composition preserved.** Observed: step 6 places the scene-kit socket under the tray (not framed), step 7 chains `verify` in the tray row with a `pass` chip, step 9 draws the frame. Screenshots `wide-step6.png`, `wide-step9.png`. Result: pass by inspection."},{"line":2322,"text":"- **Attribution: bottom-right, labelled, linked; no top-left brand.** Observed: link `made by and-scene` to `https://github.com/Codagent-AI/and-scene` at bottom-right (screenshots); brand slot empty (`data-presentation-brand-slot` has no content). Result: pass."},{"line":2323,"text":"- **Present and browse modes.** Predicted: present shows marker and title only; browse shows caption, ToC on wide, controls, progress. Observed (step 6, blurred focus, `p` key): present has marker `6` and title `It assembles the scene`, and no caption, ToC, controls, or progress elements. Browse restores them. Screenshot `s5-present.png`. Result: pass."},{"line":2324,"text":"- **Mode toggle keeps position.** Observed: step index 5 before and after toggle (present and back). Result: pass."},{"line":2325,"text":"- **Keyboard navigation.** Predicted: Right, Space, PageDown advance; Left, PageUp go back. Observed: Right 0→1, Space 1→2, PageDown 2→3, Left 3→2, PageUp 2→1. Result: pass."},{"line":2326,"text":"- **Touch swipe.** Predicted: horizontal left swipe advances, right goes back, vertical does nothing. Observed (synthetic `TouchEvent` with `Touch` objects dispatched on `window`): left swipe 5→6, right swipe 6→5, mostly-vertical gesture 5→5. Result: pass. Synthetic input stands in for a touchscreen (permitted substitute)."},{"line":2327,"text":"- **Direct jump.** Predicted: progress item jumps to that step; ToC entry jumps to the first step of that era. Observed (real clicks through AXI refs): ToC `the reveal`→8, `the gathering`→2, `the loop`→7; progress `Step 8`→7, `Step 1`→0, `Step 2`→1. Result: pass. (Note: an early progress click used a malformed uid and did nothing; it was retried with a fresh snapshot. This was a tooling error on my side, not a product failure.)"},{"line":2328,"text":"- **Active navigation state exposed.** Observed: ToC active entry has `aria-current=\"true\"` and `data-presentation-active`; progress active item has `aria-current=\"step\"` and `data-presentation-active`; both track the current era or step. (b) The sample's `.htmp [data-presentation-footer] { padding: 0 24px }` has no effect on the caption, title, or controls: the footer computes `padding-left: 24px`, but the title's `getBoundingClientRect().left` is `0`, and the caption and Previous/Next controls sit flush at x=0 at 1280 and 480 widths. Cause (code read): `Footer.tsx` places its content in an absolutely positioned wrapper with `left: 0; right: 0` inside the footer, which is itself absolutely positioned, so the footer padding is outside the wrapper's containing box. That breaks the plain wording: the helper reports an overlap warning for an element inside the marked subtree. The review guidance names this marked-versus-unmarked scenario and calls skipping any pair with at least one marked element the correct reading. So this is not an unnamed hypothetical, and the code shows the behaviour directly. The focused tests (`fx-allowed`, `fx-mixed`) only cover collisions where both elements are marked, or both are unmarked chrome. Neither covers a marked element colliding with an unmarked one, so they cannot rescue the pass.","evidence":["scripts/lib/diagnostics.mjs findOverlaps: `if (a.allow.some((id) =&gt; b.allow.includes(id))) continue` exempts a pair only when both elements share an allow-overlap ancestor; otherwise an intersecti…","collectSnapshot fills `allow` only with marked ancestors of each element, so an unmarked element has `allow = []`. A marked element colliding with it fails the skip check and gets reported.","Fixture: &#39;the helper does not report overlap warnings for elements inside that subtree&#39;. The verify copies are fine (renderRoute closes the browser in its own finally, and main&#39;s finally always calls preview.stop()), but the inspect copies alone defeat the pass verdict, whose rationale claimed cleanup covers subsequent operational errors.","evidence":["scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs and skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs: the finally block is &#39;await browser.close()&#39; followed by &#39;await preview.stop…","scripts/lib/project.mjs: the preview child is terminated (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) and awaited only inside stop().","scripts/verify.mjs: main&#39;s finally calling preview.stop() is separate from renderRoute&#39;s finally calling browser.close(), so verify is not affected. The auditor&#39;s point is that one fetch probe could stay pending, which needs a server that accepts the connection but never answers. That is a hypothetical input. The guidance does not name it, and the source and recorded evidence do not show it happening. If the preview child exits, the existing &#39;exited&#39; check and the dropped connection end the probe. The other two clauses are also met. In both verify copies, main awaits runBuild and checks its exit code before it calls startPreview. Inspect also awaits the build before starting the preview. Readiness polls HTTP rather than parsing printed output, so the ANSI and chunked-output clause does not apply.","evidence":["scripts/lib/project.mjs and the bootstrap copy: const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs with timeoutMs = 30000, and if (Date.now() &gt; deadline) throw new Error(&#39;preview not ready ...&#39;) insi…","Readiness is an HTTP probe (await fetch(url + &#39;/&#39;), break on response.ok).
